problems.title: Convert a recurring decimal
problems.question: Express 0.2(88) as a fraction.
problems.idea: Subtract two decimal expansions with identical repeating tails.

problems.title: A nested square-root domain
problems.question: Find the real domain of y=√(−√(−x)).
problems.idea: Every square-root radicand must be nonnegative.
steps: Therefore x=0, which also satisfies the first condition.

problems.title: Distance from the centroid to a side
problems.question: The altitude to a triangle side is 18. Find the centroid’s distance to that side.
problems.idea: The centroid divides a median in ratio 2:1 from the vertex.
formulas: Distance to the opposite side is one third of the corresponding altitude.
steps: Along a median, distance to its base changes linearly.
The centroid is one third of the way from the side midpoint toward the vertex, so its distance is 18/3.

problems.title: Pair absolute values about a middle point
problems.question: Evaluate |1−√199|+|2−√199|+⋯+|28−√199|.
problems.idea: Since 14<√199<15, exactly half the terms have each sign.

problems.title: A bisector and a parallel through its foot
problems.question: In ABC, B=120°, BK bisects B, KD∥AB with D on BC. AB=3, BD=2. Find BC.
problems.idea: Combine similar triangles with the angle-bisector theorem.
steps: Write BC=t. Then CK/CA=t/(t+3). Also CD/CB=(t−2)/t.

problems.title: A square-root inequality
problems.question: Solve √(−3x−2)<1.
problems.idea: Require a nonnegative radicand, then square.
steps: The left condition gives x≤−2/3; the right gives x>−1.

problems.title: Recognize an absolute value
problems.question: Find the sum of the roots of √(x²+4−4x)=3.
problems.idea: The radicand is a perfect square.

problems.title: Intersect two division segments
problems.question: In parallelogram ABCD, BM:MC=3:1, AN:ND=1:2. AM and BN meet at K. Find BK:KN.
problems.idea: Use vectors in the directions AB and AD.
formulas: Set A=0, B=u, D=v, M=u+3v/4, N=v/3.
steps: On AM, K=t(u+3v/4). On BN, K=(1−s)u+sv/3.
Equate coefficients: t=1−s and 3t/4=s/3. Thus 9(1−s)=4s, so s=9/13.

problems.title: Real square roots force a zero product
problems.question: Given √(xy)=√x·√(−y), which listed statement must hold?
problems.idea: First impose the domains of all three roots.
steps: The first two conditions imply xy≤0, while the third gives xy≥0.
Hence xy=0. Conversely this is compatible with the equality.

problems.title: Read an inequality from a shaded graph
problems.question: The boundary crosses the axes at (3,0),(0,2), and the region above it is shaded. Find the inequality.
problems.idea: Write the intercept form of the line.

problems.title: A section point between opposite sides of a line
problems.question: E,F are on opposite sides of a line at distances 1.2,1.8. ET:TF=1:4. Find T’s distance to the line.
problems.idea: Use signed distances, interpolating one fifth of the way from E to F.
steps: d(T)=(4.8−1.8)/5=0.6. Its absolute value is the distance.

problems.title: Denest two square roots
problems.question: Evaluate √(16+6√7)+√(32−10√7).
problems.idea: Recognize squares of sums and differences.

problems.title: A double inequality
problems.question: Solve −4≤1−(x−2)/3≤−3.
problems.idea: Perform each operation on all three parts.

problems.title: A tangent and the nearest circle point
problems.question: An external point A is 2 cm from the nearest circle point; its tangent length is 2√6 cm. Find the radius.
problems.idea: The center, tangency point and A form a right triangle.

problems.title: Subtract two conjugate fractions
problems.question: Evaluate $\frac{\sqrt3}{\sqrt{4+\sqrt3}+2}-\frac{\sqrt3}{\sqrt{4+\sqrt3}-2}$.
problems.idea: Combine using the difference of squares.

problems.title: Order three radical expressions
problems.question: Order a=√2+√7, b=5−√2, c=√11−√3 increasingly.
problems.idea: Use bounds sufficiently far apart to establish the order.

problems.title: Circumradius of half a rhombus
problems.question: A rhombus has AC=16, BD=8. Find the circumradius of triangle BCD.
problems.idea: Its perpendicular diagonals give the side and area.

problems.title: An integer below a negative radical
problems.question: Find the greatest integer smaller than √48−√75.
problems.idea: Simplify like radicals.
steps: Since −2<−√3<−1, the greatest integer below it is −2.

problems.title: A median cuts another segment
problems.question: M lies on AB with AM:MB=3:2. The median BK meets MC at T. Find MT:TC.
problems.idea: Use coordinates along the triangle sides.
steps: T=(1−s)3u+sv on MC; on BK write T=5(1−t)u+tv/2.

problems.title: Count integer inradii for a fixed perimeter
problems.question: An isosceles trapezoid has an incircle and perimeter 100. How many positive integer radii can occur?
problems.idea: Opposite side sums agree in a tangential quadrilateral.
formulas: Base sum=leg sum=50, so each leg=25. Height=2r≤25.
steps: Each occurs: choose half the base difference √(625−4r²); bases are 25 plus and minus that number and remain positive.

problems.title: Incompatible half-planes
problems.question: For which p does px+9y≥27, 9x+py≥18 have no solution?
problems.idea: Only parallel boundaries can prevent intersection.
steps: If p≠±9 the boundary lines intersect, providing a solution. For p=9 both are lower bounds on x+y, so compatible.
For p=−9, the inequalities give −9x+9y≥27 and 9x−9y≥18. Adding requires 0≥45.

problems.title: Expand a square with radicals
problems.question: Integers a,b satisfy (3√20−2√15)²=a+b√3. Find a+b.
problems.idea: Expand the square and simplify √300.

problems.title: When one inequality implies another
problems.question: Find every a such that each solution of 3x+a>1 also satisfies x−2>a.
problems.idea: Compare the lower endpoints of the two open intervals.
steps: Every first solution satisfies the second exactly when its lower endpoint is at least a+2.

problems.title: Two secants from the same vertex
problems.question: A circle through A,C crosses BA at M and BC at N. MB+BN=5, AM=2, NC=3. Find MB:BN.
problems.idea: Use equal powers of B.
steps: Let BM=m, BN=n, so m+n=5 and m(m+2)=n(n+3).

problems.title: Medians and a parallel in a right triangle
problems.question: In right ABC with hypotenuse AB, medians AK,CM meet at T. Through the midpoint O of AK, draw ON∥CM meeting AB at N. If MN=1, find CT.
problems.idea: Find the fraction MN/AB using vectors.
steps: Writing N=O+t(u+v)/2 and requiring its u,v coefficients to total 1 gives t=1/4.
Thus N=5u/8+3v/8, so MN=AB/8=1 and AB=8.
In a right triangle CM=AB/2=4, and CT=(2/3)CM.
